A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Generative Relightable Avatars and contain 30 readable pages, including Appendices A–L. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison; the appendix pages are unchanged.

before.justification: v1 reports original relighting experiments, baseline comparisons and ablations in Section 4 and Appendices G and J, including Tables 1–2 and 5–6.

after.justification: v2 retains the original quantitative comparisons, qualitative demonstrations and ablation results reported in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: Microfacet rendering, RelightNet, generative refinement, atemporal conditioning and error recycling are unchanged. The added RHC comparison in Section 3.2 explains the existing input distinction without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same RHC subjects and Laval lighting environments. Novel-motion/viewpoint evaluation, OLAT and near-field lighting, texture editing and few-shot adaptation coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Relighting4D, IntrinsicAvatar, MeshAvatar and DNF-Avatar. Table 6 retains both RHC variants, and the Neural Gaffer comparison remains in Table 2; no comparator membership changes.

E3.justification: The 37/3 camera split, 17-frame evaluation windows, every-tenth-frame image evaluation and every-200-frame FVD sampling remain identical. Training, tracking-robustness and few-shot adaptation protocols in the appendices are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The component, attention, pretrained-prior, few-shot, tracking-error and error-recycling analyses are unchanged in Section 4.2 and Appendix G. The same near-field relighting and texture-editing demonstrations remain.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including Appendix F's runtime averaging over 100 runs. No seed disclosures, confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated-training information are added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 1–2 and 4–6, Figure 9's trends and the qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 6 retains GRA's 30.49 PSNR, 6.42 LPIPS, 87.52 SSIM and 48.79 FVD.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12 and their assumptions and mathematical reasoning are retained. Naming LFM explicitly beside its citation changes exposition, not the flow-matching formulation.

C1.justification: The hybrid-avatar, perceptual-quality, lighting-generalization and long-video contributions retain their scope. Removing 'strong' from the introduction's qualitative out-of-distribution claim is a wording adjustment.

C2.justification: The explanations of perceptual gains, physical generalization and identity adaptation remain unchanged. Appendix L retains the same limitations concerning temporal color jitter, runtime and face/hand detail.

D1.justification: The appendices retain identical architecture, hyperparameter, hardware, training, runtime and post-processing disclosures. The project-page link is unchanged, and the Section 3.2 clarification supplies no previously undisclosed implementation setting.

R1.justification: The same 51 works are cited; publication metadata updates do not change reference membership. Section 3.2's added RHC contrast restates the image-conditioned versus pose-driven distinction already explained in Appendix J.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short RHC clarification in Section 3.2, names authors or methods beside several citations, lightly edits a contribution statement and updates bibliographic entries. Section organization and appendix prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Text reflow changes paragraph and reference page breaks and shifts Figure 5 downward. Figure 4 is recompressed while retaining its examples and lighting insets; figure/table structures and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added Section 3.2 explanation places the existing distinction from RHC directly beside the RelightNet description, making the architectural reuse and differing inputs easier to understand. Together with small citation and wording edits, this provides a limited improvement in exposition; the scientific evidence and limitations are unchanged.
